samples.summary: Access-control proxy duplicated near-verbatim from packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts instead of being shared
samples.evidence: `readOnlyNoteStore` reproduces `readOnlyDocStore` almost line for line: the same readers-allowlist rationale, the same memoized `members` map, the same non-configurable/non-writable `get` exception, and the identical `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps (compare packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:74-168). The only structural differences are the reader set, the `HISTORY_METHODS` null-returning branch, and the new `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` idempotence WeakSet — which the docs copy does NOT have, so the two implementations of the same security boundary have already diverged on first commit. This repo's stated discipline is reuse (shared code in `@wafflebase/core`; Slides reuses the Docs engine). The generic part here is store-agnostic (`readOnlyStore(store, readers, overrides)`), so it could live once. Cost is not tidiness: a hole found and patched in one proxy (as the docs one already was — see docs/tasks/archive/2026/08/20260830-docs-985-loose-ends-todo.md:129, non-function forwarding) will silently not be patched in the other, and a viewer share link on the un-patched side keeps the write path.

samples.summary: Neutering `setLocalSelection` removes viewer caret presence — a collaboration behaviour change wider than the write-boundary goal
samples.evidence: The wrapper folds `setLocalSelection` into the generic `noop` ("a viewer's caret is not something a read-only mount owes its peers"). That is a product decision, not a consequence of closing the CRDT write boundary: peer carets are a documented feature of this subsystem (docs/design/notes/notes.md:213 "Presence peer cursors", :162 posRangeToIndexRange caret decorations), and after this change an editor can no longer see where a viewer-role collaborator is reading. Presence is ephemeral, never persisted with the document, so suppressing it buys nothing the document-write ban already buys. The design-doc update records the choice but does not argue for it or note the lost awareness.

samples.summary: Frontend re-wraps a store the engine already wraps, and forces `readOnlyNoteStore` into the package's public API for it
samples.evidence: `initialize()` now wraps internally (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:249), and the only thing the frontend reads through `storeRef` is `getText()` for the thumbnail (line 183). The second wrap is defence-in-depth at the cost of a new public export (packages/notes/src/index.ts:10) that the docs package deliberately does not have for `readOnlyDocStore` — an asymmetry between the two otherwise-mirrored subsystems.
